title: UsageBassoon configuration
description: Configuration file for the UsageBassoon CLI and Python library.

source_id.description: UUID namespace generated by `bassoon init`; reuse it only for environments that represent the same collection source.

backend.description: Storage backend to use. `bassoon init` writes `duckdb` by default; this setting must be present in the file.

local_database.description: Optional local DuckDB file path. Used only when `backend` is `duckdb`; otherwise ignored. `~` expands to the home directory, and relative paths resolve from the process working directory. The Linux default is `~/.local/share/usagebassoon/usagebassoon.duckdb`; other platforms use their standard user data directory.

bigquery.description: BigQuery connection settings, used when `backend` is `bigquery`.

motherduck.description: MotherDuck connection settings, used when `backend` is `motherduck`.

bin.description: Command prefix for running tokscale, including any runner arguments (for example, `npx tokscale@latest`, `bunx tokscale@latest`, or `deno x npm:tokscale@latest`). This setting overrides the `TOKSCALE_BIN` environment variable.

env.description: Additional parent environment-variable names intentionally copied into the tokscale subprocess. Values are read from the parent process; missing names are ignored. Credentials are never inherited automatically.

timeout.description: Maximum duration of one tokscale subprocess invocation, in seconds or minutes. Defaults to `180s`; schedule.interval must be greater than this timeout.

max_stdout_bytes.description: Maximum tokscale stdout captured for one command. Defaults to 67108864 bytes; output exceeding this limit terminates the subprocess.

max_stderr_bytes.description: Maximum tokscale stderr captured for one command. Defaults to 8388608 bytes; output exceeding this limit terminates the subprocess.

dataset.description: BigQuery dataset ID to use with the configured project. Required when `backend` is `bigquery`.

location.description: BigQuery dataset and job location. Defaults to `US`.

credentials_file.description: Optional service-account credentials file path. When omitted, Google Application Default Credentials are used.

maximum_bytes_billed.description: Per-job maximum bytes billed for BigQuery queries, including user-facing relation queries. Defaults to 1073741824 bytes.

timeout.description: Maximum wait for one BigQuery job or Storage Read request, in seconds or minutes. Defaults to `120s`.

database.description: MotherDuck database name without the `md:` prefix. Required when `backend` is `motherduck`.

uri.description: Google Cloud Storage snapshot archive URI.

project.description: Google Cloud project ID used by the Storage client.

credentials_file.description: Optional service-account credentials file path. When omitted, Google Application Default Credentials are used.

timeout.description: Maximum wait for one GCS request, in seconds or minutes. Defaults to `60s`; snapshots have no overall timeout.

max_retries.description: Additional persistence attempts after the first failure. Defaults to 3.

retry_initial_seconds.description: Initial exponential-backoff delay in seconds. Defaults to 1 second.

interval.description: Interval between scheduled collection attempts in minutes or hours. Defaults to `15m` when [schedule] or this setting is omitted. Must be greater than tokscale.timeout.

directory.description: Directory for active and rotated operational logs. The Linux default is `~/.local/state/usagebassoon/logs`; other platforms use their standard user log directory.

max_files.description: Number of retained log files, including the active file. Defaults to 5.

max_bytes.description: Maximum active log file size before rotation. Defaults to 5242880 bytes.

file_uri.description: Optional local path or `file://` snapshot archive URI. On Linux, snapshots default to `~/.local/share/usagebassoon/snapshots`.

max_snapshots.description: Maximum number of retained snapshots. Defaults to 3 when [snapshots] is configured.

interval.description: Optional positive snapshot cadence, such as `30m`, `12h`, or `7d`; units are minutes, hours, or days.
